language_wrapper: Consider pairs (f, g) of functions from the nonnegative integers to the nonnegative integers. Fix integers {m_terms} >= 2 and {n_max} >= 1. Assume f is globally nonincreasing on all n >= 0 and its forward differences d_n = f(n) - f(n+1) form a nondecreasing sequence with each d_n in {0, 1} (so f is flat up to some index, then drops by exactly 1 each step until it reaches 0). In addition, the budget constraint holds: f(0) + f(1) + ... + f({n_max}) <= {s_budget}. For any choice of {m_terms} nonnegative integers n_1, ..., n_{m_terms}, we have g(n_1 + ... + n_{m_terms}) <= f(n_1) + ... + f(n_{m_terms}). Determine the maximum possible value of g(0) + g(1) + ... + g({n_max}).
hardness_rationale: The seed problem constrains a nonincreasing function f with a simple budget and uses a single m-fold inequality to bound g via a worst-case (minimum) over partitions. Our augmentation generalizes the index and budget while imposing a discrete convexity structure: the forward differences of f are nondecreasing and take values in {0,1}, meaning that f is flat up to some index and then drops by exactly 1 at each step. This structure forces the minimum over all m-partitions of a fixed sum to occur at (almost) equal splits, which transforms the bound into a min-plus (tropical) convolution. Maximizing the sum of g across 0..N now requires optimizing over the shape parameters (plateau height and drop onset) subject to the budget, and evaluating the equal-split convolution for each candidate. The analysis and computation rely on majorization/Karamata-type reasoning (equalization minimizes sums for convex f), discrete convexity, and an optimization over shape space, which is significantly more intricate than the original and cannot be solved by simple guessing.
notes: Verifier searches over all admissible plateau-then-slope-1 shapes consistent with the budget to compute the optimal sum of g, using the equal-split formula for the minimal m-part sum for convex decreasing f. Generator ensures instances are nontrivial by rejecting cases where the optimal f is purely flat over [0..N].
source_question:
Consider pairs \((f, g)\) of functions from the set of nonnegative integers to itself such that \(f(0) \ge f(1) \geq f(2) \geq \cdots \ge f(2016) \ge 0\) and \(f(0)+f(1)+f(2)+\cdots +f(2016) \le 2016\). For any 20 nonnegative integers \(n_{1}, n_{2}, \dots, n_{20}\), not necessarily distinct, we have \[
g(n_{1}+n_{2}+\cdots+n_{20}) \le f(n_{1})+f(n_{2})+\cdots+f(n_{20})
\] 
Determine the maximum possible value of \(g(0)+g(1)+\cdots+g(2016)\) over all such pairs of functions.
